'''Deryck William Goodwin''' (28 September 1927 – 12 March 1997) was an English physicist, particularly researching into [[laser]]s. In later years he was an Anglican priest.

==Life==
He was born in [[Lincoln, England|Lincoln]], and was educated at [[Lincoln Grammar School|Lincoln School]]. He studied at the [[University of Birmingham]], where after graduating he completed a PhD.<ref name=obit>Obituary, "The Rev Deryck Goodwin". ''[[The Times]]'', 14 April 1997.</ref>

At the [[Royal Radar Establishment]] in [[Malvern, Worcestershire|Malvern]], he investigated [[indium antimonide]] as an [[infrared detector]]; he built a [[ruby laser]], thought to be the first ruby laser to operate in Britain, and investigated the [[spectroscopy]] of possible [[Active laser medium|laser materials]].<ref name=obit/>

He joined the academic staff of the [[University of York]] soon after its establishment, and helped to set up the undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in physics. He continued his research into lasers, investigating materials for lasers, and possible applications. He wrote articles in newspapers and magazines about laser technology and its importance outside scientific research.<ref name=obit/>

Goodwin was [[ordained]] as an Anglican priest in 1978, and for nine years was a [[Non-Stipendiary Minister|non-stipendiary curate]] at [[Elvington, North Yorkshire|Elvington]], near York. He retired from the university in 1986, and became vicar of [[Burton Pidsea]], near Hull. He was afterwards rector of Middleton with Newton, Levisham and Lockton in [[North Yorkshire]], until retirement in 1994.<ref name=obit/><ref>[https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/church-appointments-1371860.html "Church appointments"] ''[[The Independent]]'', 23 April 1994. Retrieved 23 August 2025.</ref>

He advised about the lighting of churches, and set up Goodwin Lighting, a voluntary consultancy. The service, initially in the [[Diocese of York]], spread beyond the region and included [[Lincoln Cathedral]],  [[Westminster Abbey]] and [[Fountains Abbey]].<ref name=obit/><ref>[https://lincolnchristshospitalschool.co.uk/_documents/%5B1017560%5DOccasional_Paper_11_Looking_Back.pdf "Looking Back"]  Occasional Paper No 11 by Professor Charles Garton. Lincoln Christ’s Hospital School, April 2012. Retrieved 23 August 2025.</ref>

Goodwin died of cancer in 1997, aged 69.<ref name=obit/> His wife Joyce ''née'' Lumley, whom he married in 1988,<ref>[[FreeBMD]].</ref> died in 2013.<ref>[https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/10648015.Joyce_Elizabeth_GOODWIN/ "Joyce Elizabeth Goodwin"] ''[[The Press (York)|The Press]]'', 4 September 2013. Retrieved 23 August 2025.</ref>
